records.summary: Whether reverent or skeptical, faith plays a role in nearly every Dionasian's life: •Do you honor the gods, fear them, or question them? •Have you made a pilgrimage to a Gravity Well or First Tower? •Do you carry a gravity talisman, chant stormward prayers, or seek the silence of ravines? •Do you seek absolution for your ancestorsʼ sins—or continue their rebellion? The Faith of the Fractured Sky reminds all Dionasians that they live on borrowed stability. Faith is not about certainty—it is about survival in a world that remembers falling and has never quite stopped.

Dionasiaʼs past is defined by ambition, catastrophe, and divine intervention. What was once a vibrant, advanced world was undone in a single generation of hubris. The people who survived became stewards of a broken sky, inheritors of fallen greatness. This history is a source of reverence, warning, and unresolved mystery.

records.proposedName: Before the Fracture (The Era of Ascension)
records.summary: •Dionasia Unified: A lush, gravity-stable world with advanced societies built on the fusion of magic and machinery. •Rise of the Technomages: Scholars and inventors form powerful guilds that blend arcane and scientific disciplines. •Creation of the Ascension Machines: Massive structures designed to extract energy from the planetʼs core and pierce the divine veil. Promised to bring eternal prosperity—and control over life and death. •Spiritual Opposition: Mystic orders and religious sects warn of imbalance, but are dismissed or silenced. •Initial Signs: Birds fail to migrate, tides reverse, crops warp, and the stars begin to drift.

•You found an active technomage core humming beneath your family home. What do you do? •Youʼre offered a place in a hidden relic-forging guild. Can you keep the secret? •You received visions from an ancient AI buried beneath a ravine. Are they divine… or digital? •You wear a suit built before the Fall. It whispers to you at night. To understand Dionasia is to face the broken promise of progress: a world built to ascend, forced to survive. Technomancy is not just a lost science—it is a mirror to the soul of Dionasia itself, asking: Should we build again? And if so… who decides how high we reach?
Exploration in Dionasia is not just about where you go—itʼs how you move.

Dionasia makes a memorable stop or full campaign setting in a multiversal adventure. Travelers might: •Arrive in a Ravine Storm, stranded until they can align with a Gravity Well. •Be mistaken for gods, technomancers, or skybeast riders. •Fall into the sky, triggering a rescue mission to recover an ally caught in upward drift. •Discover a lost piece of the Ascension Machines, the technology strangely compatible with another world.

Use these to tie players to the setting: •“You were born in a low-tier slum. What did you see fall into the sky?” •“You carry a relic banned by the Skyseers. Why havenʼt you destroyed it?” •“Your dreams are filled with visions of Aserʼs tears. Do you think itʼs prophecy—or guilt?” •“A sibling joined the Ascenders. You havenʼt heard from them since.” Dionasia is a setting for adventurers who climb while the world falls, who question whether the gods were merciful or cruel, and who balance the pull of legacy with the weight of survival. Your next step might not be forward—it might be upward. Or downward. Or… both.

records.proposedName: The World Itself Is Your Enemy
records.summary: Dionasiaʼs greatest threat isnʼt always monsters—itʼs the planet itself. From shifting gravity to skyward storms, every region of this fractured world holds environmental, spiritual, and technological dangers. Survival requires knowledge, preparation, and the humility to know when to back away from the edge.

•Play With Orientation: Flip the map. Drop the floor. Use height like others use terrain. •Reward Preparation: Characters with ropes, anchors, and gliders should thrive. •Echoes Speak: Let the past bleed into the present, even when itʼs inconvenient. •Use Rituals as Tools: Religious NPCs arenʼt just flavor—they are guides to deeper truths and hidden systems. •Show Donʼt Tell the Weird: Let visuals and altered physics tell the players they are somewhere sacred… or cursed. Running Dionasia is about weaving awe with danger, verticality with tension, and memory with mystery. The world wants to fall apart. Your players must decide whatʼs worth holding onto—and what must be let go.

records.proposedName: Raised in a World That Fell Upward
records.summary: Characters from Dionasia come from a world where falling is fatal, gravity is sacred, and society clings to the remnants of a shattered planet. Whether born among the Hanging Cities or raised in the drifting ruins of pre-Fracture technomancy, Dionasians carry the burden of a broken world—and the spiritual, cultural, or technological tools to navigate it.

The are 3 systems of universities in kess Andria. The university of technology, Gray River Universities. The university of biologies, Gallowmere Universities. The university of souls, Prosperity Universities. Sometimes they work together on projects, sometimes they spy on one another and attempt sabotage. Kess Andria is a region renowned for its academic institutions. The three major universities - Gray River, Gallowmere, and Prosperity - specialize in technology, biology, and souls respectively, making the region a hub for cutting-edge research and development. However, beneath the surface of this intellectual paradise, tensions simmer. Each university is fiercely competitive and jealous of their research and knowledge, leading to occasional bouts of espionage and sabotage. Each university has its own secrets and technology, and they will do whatever it takes to keep them hidden from the others. Players can take on the role of students, faculty members, or researchers from one of the universities, navigating the politics and rivalries between them while pursuing their own goals. Maybe they're trying to uncover a conspiracy that threatens to bring down one of the universities, or they're working on a project that requires cooperation from all three universities, despite their differences. As they delve deeper into the world of academic intrigue, players will have to use their skills and knowledge to outmaneuver their rivals, avoid traps and dangers, and protect their own secrets. They may encounter powerful and dangerous technologies, ethically questionable research projects, and strange and mysterious creatures that defy explanation
“A sanctuary. A scar. A city that should never have worked. A world still holding itself together— barely.”

•Core Feature: 13 danger-ranked zones, radiating outward from the Vertigon sector •Primary City: Vertigon — economic hub, portal nexus, and fractured capital of survival and intrigue •Climate & Geography: No ice caps; warm-temperate base with wide ecological variance •Multiversal Role: Former convergence world and ecological vault, now partially unmoored •Current Status: Fragmented but stable; active political contention, ecological mutation, multiversal relevance high

“At the end of the world, all things are equal—even the mistakes.” The Riftfall Verge is multiversal entropy made manifest. Itʼs where explorers stop being tourists and become witnesses to collapse, convergence, and divergence. The zone asks players to grapple with what identity means when reality fractures—and whether you can still be you when you're not alone in your skin.

records.proposedName: The World of Heimenhearth: A Million Years of Growth
records.summary: Once a battleground of industry and war, Heimenhearth has evolved into one of the most advanced and strategically significant worlds in the Goblin Empire. While originally built by the dwarves as a massive Dyson Sphere—a megastructure encasing its sun—this artificial world has undergone a million years of development, turning it into the Portal Capital of the Empire and a hub for multiversal trade, politics, and technological innovation. The planet-sized sphere is now a layered, industrialized, and cosmopolitan world, where ancient dwarven machinery, goblin economic prowess, and elven magic-infused technology coexist in a delicate but powerful balance. While its origins were forged in war and greed, modern Heimenhearth is the beating heart of the empireʼs interdimensional infrastructure—an irreplaceable nexus that connects the multiverse like no other world.

records.proposedName: The Evolution of Starforge: From War to Trade
records.summary: Originally referred to as Starforge, the name of the Tales Industries mega-factory that dominated its skyline, Heimenhearth was initially nothing more than a dwarven-built machine, created to harness the full power of its star through massive energy collection systems. Its people—mostly dwarves— relentlessly mined the systemʼs planets and moons, using them as raw materials to construct the Dyson Sphereʼs layers of industry and infrastructure. However, this relentless expansion led to war. The elves of Elaria, a neighboring world rich in the mystical metal Orilaun, suffered catastrophic destruction when the dwarves stripped their planet of its core. This triggered the Orilaun Wars, an event that saw the first major multiversal war fought over magic, technology, and power. The elves, nearly wiped out, took to the stars on the Etherflotilla, a fleet of massive, living bioships. Meanwhile, the dwarves suffered their first real losses when their megastructure was fractured by elven counterattacks, leaving behind the Shattered Zone—a ruined sector still haunted by ancient defenses and reality-bending anomalies. Despite this destruction, Heimenhearth endured. Over time, as the goblins rose to power in the early days of the Empire, the sphere shifted from being a purely dwarven industrial world to a multiversal trade hub. The goblins, experts in finance, logistics, and economic warfare, recognized Heimenhearthʼs potential and transformed it into the Empireʼs single most important portal hub, where the multiversal economy, portal travel, and technological expansion could thrive. Now, a million years later, Heimenhearth stands not as a war machine, but as an economic titan—the largest, most efficient trade and transportation hub in the Empire.

Over the course of a million years, Heimenhearth has become the technological backbone of the Goblin Empire, a hub of industry, multiversal travel, and war machine production. The combination of dwarven engineering, goblin financial control, and elven Orilaun research has made Heimenhearth the most advanced world in the Empire, responsible for portal infrastructure, starship development, and mecha warfare.

records.proposedName: Old Vitoria (Southern Part of the Continent)
records.summary: Cultural Hub: Being in the southern, more temperate region, Old Vitoria could be the historical and cultural heartland, rich in traditions, arts, and literature. Agricultural Prosperity: Fertile lands would allow for diverse agriculture, making it a breadbasket region with a cuisine rich in grains, fruits, and vegetables. Architectural Heritage: Old Vitoria might boast historical architecture, with grand buildings and monuments that speak to its long and storied past. Merchant Traditions: Its location could make it a center for trade, with a strong tradition of commerce and a diverse, cosmopolitan populace.

Cultural Blending: Following unification, these diverse regions would have experienced significant cultural exchange, leading to a richly diverse national identity. Economic and Political Integration: The distinct economic strengths of each region would contribute to Vitoria's overall economic robustness and diversity. Balancing Regional Identities: One of the key challenges post-unification would be balancing these regional identities and ensuring equitable development and representation across the new nation. Formerly a dictatorship, Vitoria is transitioning to a parliamentary democracy under the guidance of Viktor Caepheus, a benevolent leader who succeeded his father. His genuine efforts to empower the people mark a stark contrast to the nation's authoritarian past. The orcish arrival poses a unique challenge to Vitoria's political transition, potentially impacting the newly forming democratic processes and their relationship with other nations. Early Period (200-100 years before incursion): Vitoria was under a stable but rigid authoritarian regime. The government maintained strict control over the nation, with limited civic freedoms. The society was orderly, but there was an undercurrent of desire for change. Later Period (100-0 years before incursion): Gradual political shifts began as new ideas and demands for reform emerged. The nation started moving towards a more participatory form of governance, setting the stage for the eventual transition to democracy.

Omniversum presents a branch where seamless travel and cultural interplay are the norm. Its mechanics emphasize mobility, trade, hybrid technology, and the challenges of managing a multiverse that feels like a tightly knit community. Players will experience a world thatʼs both diverse and deeply connected, making for campaigns that flow naturally while offering a wide variety of opportunities.

records.proposedName: The Unreal Zone: Overview and Key Features
records.summary: The Unreal Zone (UZ) is a chaotic and whimsical branch of the multiverse, defined by its rejection of conventional logic and its embrace of exaggerated, surreal, and often cartoonish physics. This branch is not only a place of unpredictable adventure but also a realm that challenges the very perceptions and stability of those who dare to enter it.

•Cells of Conceptual Isolation: Each inmate is contained in a pocket-reality cell tailored to their archetype. •Loop Suppressors: Prevents recursive behavior unless authorized for study. •Narrative Dampeners: Limit toon abilities like “pop back up” healing or dimension-shifting. •Emergency Killjoy Protocol: Entire prison can switch to grayscale “serious mode,” disabling most cartoon logic for 10 minutes.

The overgrown city is a place of danger and the unknown. Use random encounters and hazards to keep players on edge, emphasizing the unpredictability of the terrain. This Post-Apocalyptic Overgrown City guide equips GMs and players with everything needed to navigate a world of decayed infrastructure and reclaimed wilderness. With its mix of urban ruins and dense foliage, the overgrown city challenges players to adapt and survive, presenting unique opportunities for exploration, resourcefulness, and discovery.

records.proposedName: The Spine of the World (Tundra World -142)
records.summary: A buried serpent skeleton the size of a city, turned into a crypt-temple. Followers slowly merge into its bones during rites. Hook: Every 13 years, the temple “sheds,” and a new high priest is born from within the spine. •
The world of Sharra indeed presents a captivating setting. To deepen the exploration of this world, let's delve further into the societies and characters of the different regions and inhabitants.

- Location: Beneath the ice of the Great Glacial Expanse. - Description: A vast repository of knowledge, housing scrolls, texts, and artifacts from millennia of Sharr history. By further exploring these cities and landmarks within the compelling icy realms of Laurasia, the rich tapestry of the Sharr society and their harmonious existence within this frigid world is brought to vivid life.

Gondwana is a vast, verdant continent where the ancient thrum of life vibrates through the air, ground, and waters. Flourishing flora and fauna, from towering fern forests to the magnificent dinosaurs, paint a landscape echoing the primordial epochs of Earth.

- Location: Scattered across the Saurian Plains. - Description: Ancient burial and ceremonial sites, where the bones of mighty dinosaurs and revered Traiga rest intertwined. Gondwanaʼs rich and ancient terrain, populated by the agile and harmonious Traiga, whispers tales of primal bonds, audacious hunts, and the timeless dance of life and nature. The pulsating beat of the continent echoes in the hunt calls of the Traiga and the thunderous steps of the dinosaurs, reverberating under the vast, azure skies.

records.proposedName: The Deep Blue: Home of the Kola-Ha
records.summary: The world beneath the waves, where the Kola-Ha reign, is a realm of breathtaking beauty and inherent peril. An endless ocean teeming with myriad life forms, from the tiniest plankton to the gargantuan leviathans of the deep. Vibrant coral reefs, mysterious abysses, and sprawling kelp forests define this boundless underwater world.
